subject: Data holding TTL and rapid erase guidance for Hosted API
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@greenwavehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@greenwavehealth.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on data holding TTL + rapid erasure for hosted API

Hi Jordan,

We are completing our security questionnaire and need clarifications on how Redwood handles data for the hosted API with respect to retention, what is included in erasure requests, and how quickly erasure can be effected in case of an incident. Specifics we need:

1) What categories of data are retained (raw request, model output, logs, embeddings, telemetry) and default TTLs?
2) Are there backups or cold archives outside the primary store that would extend recovery windows?
3) If we request emergency erasure for a tenant (legal/personal data), what is the scope and SLA for completion and verification?
4) Any options to opt-out of retention or change TTLs for our account in hosted mode?

Please include high-level steps you take operationally when you process an erasure and any artifacts (audit log, ticket id) we can expect.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morales
Senior InfoSec Manager
GreenWave Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@greenwavehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 12:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on data holding TTL + rapid erasure for hosted API

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I included Karthik (platform) and Marissa (legal/compliance) for operational details and verification artifacts.

Summary (short):
- Default retention: request payloads (prompts), model outputs, and request metadata are retained up to 30 days by default for debugging, abuse detection, and quality monitoring.
- Embeddings and derived artifacts: treated as customer data; default 30-day TTL unless otherwise contracted.
- Telemetry/metrics: aggregated telemetry retained longer (90 days) and is anonymized; not used to reconstruct specific prompts.
- Backups: we maintain short-term backup copies to support disaster recovery; backups are immutable for a limited window (up to 7 days) and are included in erasure scope.
- Emergency erasure SLA: standard hosted erasure requests are completed within 3 business days; emergency/incident-driven erasures are targeted within 24–72 hours depending on scope.
- Opt-outs/config: customers can request a retention-restricted profile (no persistent storage of request/response bodies) for hosted API under an add-on contract; Dedicated/Private deployments offer more granular controls.

Operational steps (top-level):
1) Customer submits erasure request (Support ticket or API-based request).
2) We validate identity and scope with the customer (ticket).
3) Platform applies TTL override & initiates purge across primary stores, KV caches, and backup index within SLA.
4) Post-purge, we run a verification job that searches indexes and copies for residual objects and generate an audit record (ticket id + purge run id).
5) We provide a signed deletion confirmation and the audit record for your records.

Attachments: I attached a short diagram of our data flow and a one-page summary of the erasure playbook. Karthik will follow up with technical notes on what exactly is removed in each layer.

Next steps: If GreenWave needs a shorter retention window by default or a no-persistence hosted profile, tell me and I'll route to procurement/ops for a change-order.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): hostedapi-data-flow-diagram.pdf, erasure-playbook-summary.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@greenwavehealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 10:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on data holding TTL + rapid erasure for hosted API (technical detail)

Hi Elena — adding the technical breakdown you asked for. I'll keep it succinct and operational.

What we retain by default (examples):
- Request bodies (raw prompt): retained in primary object store for 30 days.
- Model outputs (completions): retained for 30 days alongside request object.
- Request metadata (time, model_id, tokens used, route): retained for 30 days.
- Embeddings/derived vectors: treated as customer-owned objects; retained 30 days unless contractually changed.
- KV caches and ephemeral caches: cached only in-memory or short-lived disk backing with TTLs aligned to requests (default cache eviction within 1–2 hours); not part of primary retention except for warm cache snapshots used for autoscaling (these are rotated and expire within 48 hours).
- Aggregated telemetry/metrics: time-series (no PII) kept 90 days.

Backups and snapshots:
- Short-term immutable snapshots exist for up to 7 days to support recovery operations.
- Long-term archival (cold storage) is not used for request/response data in hosted mode.

Erasure scope and mechanics:
- Scope: raw request bodies, completions, embeddings, indexing keys, associated metadata, and any snapshot that contains the objects.
- Mechanic: the purge job marks objects for deletion, expunges from indexes, triggers background workers to remove shard copies, and submits deletions to backup/replica systems.
- SLA: Standard: completion and verification artifact within 72 hours. Emergency: 24 hours target for scoped tenant-level deletes — we run a prioritized pipeline and confirm with an audit token.

Verification & artifacts you get back:
- Deletion run id (e.g., DR-20260616-4572)
- Support ticket id linking to logs of the purge run (no raw content in ticket)
- MD5 hashes of objects removed where allowed (to prove removal of specific keys)
- Time-stamped audit log entries showing wipe operations and operator ids (redacted where necessary)

Limitations/notes:
- If data has been exported by the customer (downstream copies) Redwood cannot purge customer-managed copies.
- For legal holds invoked by subpoena we will surface the required process via legal; that can pause an erasure until hold is resolved.

If you want, I can schedule a short tech walk-through and show the verification PDF we produce for each purge.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Platform Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on data holding TTL + rapid erasure for hosted API (confirmation & legal)

Hi Elena — quick legal confirmation:

- The operational description Karthik provided aligns with our standard hosted terms. We can provide a retention addendum to set a default TTL shorter than 30 days (e.g., 7 days) or a "no-persistence" hosted profile as a contract amendment.
- When we deliver the deletion confirmation we include a signed attestation referencing the support ticket and deletion run id; this satisfies typical audit/evidence requests.
- We will not include raw content in the attestation (to protect operator and system security), but we can provide object identifiers and hashes for verification where allowed.

If GreenWave wants the retention addendum I'll prepare a short SOW and pricing for the retention-restricted hosted profile.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference
